title: Compatibility of the Kunneth map with Leray, proper base change and the projection formula
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $f:X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $g:Y\to S$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Put $W=X\times_S Y$, with projections $p:W\to X$, $q:W\to Y$ and $c=fp=gq$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

(a) Assume that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, let $E\in D^+(X_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ have torsion cohomology [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], and let $K\in D^+(Y_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

(b) Alternatively, let $n\ge1$ be invertible in $k$, set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, let $Y$ be of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be arbitrary, possibly unbounded.

In either case use ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and unbounded derived global sections [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]; identify the derived category of module sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ with $D(\Lambda)$ by evaluation at $S$. Put
$$A=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E),\qquad B=R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K),\qquad F=p^{-1}E,\qquad T=F\otimes^L_\Lambda q^{-1}K.$$
Let $\sigma_{U,V}:U\otimes^L_\Lambda V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes^L_\Lambda U$ denote the canonical symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. Identify $g^{-1}A$ with the constant complex $\underline A$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Write
$$e:g^{-1}A\longrightarrow Rq_*F$$
for the canonical exchange morphism [def-kun-unbounded-exchange],
$$t=\mathrm{PF}_q(F,K):Rq_*F\otimes^L_\Lambda K\longrightarrow Rq_*T$$
for the projection-formula morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and
$$r=\mathrm{PF}_{Y,\Lambda}(K,A):B\otimes^L_\Lambda A\longrightarrow R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline A)$$
for the constant-coefficient projection morphism [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Let
$$\ell:R\Gamma(W_{\Et},T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*T)$$
be the canonical Leray composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. All these maps are computed in the full unbounded derived categories; bounded-below isomorphism assertions in (a) are interpreted through their canonical inclusions.

The arrows $e,t,r$ are isomorphisms: in (a) their isomorphism assertions are respectively [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], [lem-kun-0f0f], [lem-kun-0f0e]; in (b) they are respectively [lem-kun-0f0c], [lem-kun-0f0g], [lem-kun-0f12]. Define the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta:R\Gamma(W_{\Et},T)
&\xrightarrow{\ell} R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*T)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,t^{-1})}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*F\otimes^L_\Lambda K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,e^{-1}\otimes1)}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},\underline A\otimes^L_\Lambda K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,\sigma_{\underline A,K})}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline A)\\
&\xrightarrow{r^{-1}}B\otimes^L_\Lambda A
\xrightarrow{\sigma_{B,A}}A\otimes^L_\Lambda B.
\end{aligned}$$
Then $\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=1_{A\otimes^L_\Lambda B}$ for the canonical Kunneth map [def-kun-kunneth-map]; consequently $\kappa_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\theta$.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-0ezp], every object of the small étale site of $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a disjoint union of copies of $S$. Since $k$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed], it has no nontrivial finite separable extension, so every separable algebraic extension of $k$ (a union of finite separable ones) is $k$ itself: $k^{\rm sep}=k$ and $G=\operatorname{Gal}(k/k)$ is trivial. Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega\supseteq k$ and the geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] with $K=k$ says that the geometric stalk at $\bar s$ is an additive equivalence from abelian sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ to discrete $G$-modules, i.e. (as $G=1$) to all abelian groups; an additive equivalence of abelian categories is exact. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules] with the finite ring $A=\Lambda$ gives the exact equivalence of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ with $\Lambda[G]$-modules, i.e. $\Lambda$-modules, sections corresponding to invariants, i.e. to the whole stalk. In both cases the global-section-to-germ map $F(S)\to F_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $F$: an étale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar s$ has $U=\coprod S$, $\bar u$ lies on one component, and the inclusion of that component is a morphism of neighbourhoods $(S,\bar s)\to(U,\bar u)$, so $(S,\bar s)$ is cofinal in the colimit defining the stalk. Hence evaluation $\mathrm{ev}(F)=F(S)$ is an exact $\Lambda$-linear equivalence $\Mod(S_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(\Lambda)$. Next, sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] does not change the value at $S$: for a presheaf $P$ of $\Lambda$-modules and a sheaf $F$, a morphism $P\to F$ is the same as a $\Lambda$-linear map $P(S)\to F(S)$, because $F(U)=\prod F(S)$ over the components of $U=\coprod S$ (sheaf axiom for the covering by the pairwise disjoint components) and every $S$-morphism between disjoint unions of copies of $S$ maps each component identically onto a component ($\operatorname{Aut}_S(S)=\{1\}$). By the universal property and full faithfulness of $\mathrm{ev}$ on sheaves, the canonical map $P(S)\to P^{\#}(S)$ is an isomorphism. Applied to the constant presheaf with value $M$, this gives $\mathrm{ev}(\underline M)=M$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], so the constant-sheaf functor is the quasi-inverse of $\mathrm{ev}$ with identity unit; applied to the presheaf tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (here $\Lambda_S(S)=\Lambda$), it gives $\mathrm{ev}(F\otimes_{\Lambda_S}G)=F(S)\otimes_\Lambda G(S)$ with $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$. Applying $\mathrm{ev}$ termwise, it commutes with total tensor complexes and with acyclicity in both directions, hence carries K-flat complexes to K-flat complexes; so it induces an equivalence $D(S_{\Et},\Lambda)\simeq D(\Lambda)$, preserving cohomological lower bounds, which is monoidal for the ordinary derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor] with tensor comparison $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$ on representatives. All module structures and restrictions are componentwise.

proof.text: Using the monoidal equivalence $\mathrm{ev}$ of step 1 and the definition [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded], together with $(g_*G)(S)=G(Y\times_SS)=G(Y)$ for the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (and likewise for $f$), evaluation at the terminal object identifies $R_fE$ with $A$ and $R_gK$ with $B$, while [lem-kun-pullback-constant] identifies $L_gA$ with the constant complex $\underline A$. The ordinary $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ Hom bijection is the constant-sheaf/global-sections bijection under these componentwise equivalences; its counit sends a constant label to the corresponding section. The tensor comparison sends constant labels to their tensor, so by [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] it is exactly the projection morphism $r$ after passage to derived categories using [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: Proof paragraph, the sentence identifying the constant-object map [lem-kun-pullback-constant] and the fourth mate (constant projection) of $\theta$.

proof.text: The module categories $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ for $T=S,Y,W$ are Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and $g^{-1},q^{-1},c^{-1}$ are exact additive left adjoints of $g_*,q_*,c_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; so [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] applies with $L_a=g^{-1}$, $L_b=q^{-1}$, $L_c=c^{-1}$ and $\lambda$ the module composition isomorphism $q^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}c^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], clause (2), whose conjugate is the direct-image composition isomorphism $c_*\cong g_*q_*$ by that lemma's final clause. Apply the canonical derived pushforward comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $\ell:R_cT\to R_gR_qT$. Its K-injective normalization, together with [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], identifies this comparison with the conjugate of the composite derived adjunction for $L_qL_g\dashv R_gR_q$, so its units and counits are the composite ones specified by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] says that the canonical module inverse-image composition map carries the composite unit to the single-map unit. Therefore transposing through $\ell$ is exactly the single-map $c^{-1}\dashv R_c$ transpose used in [def-kun-kunneth-map].

source.place: Proof paragraph, the sentence beginning 'Each arrow in the definition of $\theta$ is the mate of an identification built from the adjunction data'.

proof.text: Use $\otimes$ for $\otimes^L_\Lambda$. We will suppress the canonical comparisons $L_u(U\otimes V)\cong L_uU\otimes L_uV$ of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], but check their compatibility with composition and symmetry. For the canonical module composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], clause (2), either order of successive inverse images sends a local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the two successively pulled-back labels. The inverse-image composition identification therefore respects the two tensor factors; the two maps agree on local generators, hence on sheaves. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives using the equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the constant-coefficient module pullback $u^*$ is canonically $u^{-1}$ and is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], its termwise application preserves K-flatness and flat terms; exactness preserves the chosen resolution quasi-isomorphisms. The original models and all their successive pullbacks therefore compute the derived tensors by [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the canonical comparison is the ordinary comparison in every bidegree. The same local-label calculation applies to the square isomorphism $L_qL_g\cong L_pL_f$: each route pulls back each of the two labels along the equal composite $c$. The symmetry multiplies bidegree $(i,j)$ by $(-1)^{ij}$, which is unchanged by inverse image and by composition. Both routes have differential $d\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d$. Thus the equations hold on these models. The two-variable determination of natural transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extends these equations to the full derived categories. This proves precisely the tensor/composition and tensor/symmetry identifications used below; it does not infer them from an exchange-pasting theorem. The symmetry is the canonical one of [lem-kun-tensor-sym].

proof.text:
Define $s:A\otimes B\to R_g(L_gA\otimes K)$ by
$$s=R_g(\sigma_{K,L_gA})\circ r\circ\sigma_{A,B}.$$
By [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], the $g$-adjoint of $r$ is $\varepsilon_{g,K}\otimes1_{L_gA}$. By the adjunction identification in step 2 this is the $g$-adjunction used here. Naturality and involutivity of the signed symmetry checked in step 4 give the explicit equality
$$\sigma_{K,L_gA}(\varepsilon_{g,K}\otimes1_{L_gA})\sigma_{L_gA,L_gB}=1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K}.$$
Thus [lem-kun-tensor-sym] and the adjunct-counit identity give
$$\varepsilon_{g,L_gA\otimes K}\,L_g(s)=1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K}.$$
For $F=L_pE$, the definitions [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and [def-kun-projection-formula-map] give, respectively,
$$\varepsilon_{q,F}L_q(e)=L_p(\varepsilon_{f,E}):L_qL_gA\cong L_pL_fA\to F,$$
$$\varepsilon_{q,T}L_q(t)=\varepsilon_{q,F}\otimes1_{L_qK}.$$
Each equality is just the adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], applied to the specific adjoint written in the cited definition; all source tensor identifications are those checked in step 4. No map is assumed invertible in these equalities.

proof.text:
Put $U=L_gA\otimes K$, $m=t\circ(e\otimes1_K):U\to R_qT$, and
$$v=R_g(m)\circ s:A\otimes B\longrightarrow R_gR_qT,\qquad \lambda=\ell^{-1}\circ v.$$
Naturality of the counit for the morphism $m$ says
$$\varepsilon_{g,R_qT}\,L_gR_g(m)=m\,\varepsilon_{g,U}.$$
Consequently the $g$-adjoint of $v$ is $m(1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K})$, by step 5. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and the normalization checked in step 3, make the $c$-adjoint of $\lambda$ the following typed morphism:
$$L_qL_g(A\otimes B)\xrightarrow{L_q(1\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K})}L_qU\xrightarrow{L_q(e\otimes1)}L_q(R_qF\otimes K)\xrightarrow{L_qt}L_qR_qT\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{q,T}}T.$$
This is obtained by applying the Hom bijections, whose inverse is the counit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity]; no unit is moved past a tensor without the naturality already checked.

proof.text:
Substitute the projection identity from step 5 into this $c$-adjoint. Bifunctoriality of the tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] turns its final two arrows into $\varepsilon_{q,F}\otimes1_{L_qK}$. Composing with $L_q(e\otimes1)$ and the first arrow then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda^\flat
&=(\varepsilon_{q,F}L_qe)\otimes L_q(\varepsilon_{g,K})\\
&=L_p(\varepsilon_{f,E})\otimes L_q(\varepsilon_{g,K}):
L_c(A\otimes B)\cong L_pL_fA\otimes L_qL_gB\longrightarrow L_pE\otimes L_qK=T.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is the exchange identity from step 5. To compare with the current [def-kun-kunneth-map] without suppressing its source comparisons, write $\mu^c_{A,B}:L_cA\otimes L_cB\xrightarrow{\sim}L_c(A\otimes B)$ and use that definition's $\gamma_{f,p}:L_c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_pL_f$ and $\gamma_{g,q}:L_c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_qL_g$. The preceding computation says explicitly that $\lambda^\flat=(L_p\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes L_q\varepsilon_{g,K})\circ(\gamma_{f,p,A}\otimes\gamma_{g,q,B})\circ(\mu^c_{A,B})^{-1}$. The module composition maps in step 3 are precisely these $\gamma$ maps, and the tensor comparison is the inverse of the same canonical $\mu^c$. This is exactly the $\alpha_{E,K}$ whose adjunct defines $\kappa_{E,K}$ in [def-kun-kunneth-map], using the same K-injective Hom bijection and ordinary counits as in step 2. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection therefore proves $\lambda=\kappa_{E,K}$. In particular this argument works for all commutative coefficient rings and unbounded complexes; properness and finiteness are needed only to make its factors invertible.

proof.text: For (a), $q$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. The exact additive inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves bounded-below complexes. It preserves torsion cohomology by the existing statement [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion], applied degreewise to the cohomology sheaves of $E$. Therefore $F=p^{-1}E$ has the boundedness and torsion hypotheses required by [lem-kun-0f0f], so $t$ is invertible.

The hypotheses of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] hold for $(f,g,E)$, so its exchange isomorphism gives $e$. By [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees], the bounded exchange is the restriction of the unbounded exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]: both have the same transpose $L_p\varepsilon_f$ under the normalized derived adjunction. Thus the $e$ used in the common-adjoint calculation is exactly the canonical unbounded map, not merely an isomorphic endpoint.

To apply the constant projection theorem, $A$ is bounded below. The enough-injectives and bounded-below representative nodes [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] provide a bounded-below K-injective representative $I$ of $E$; termwise sections in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] have the same lower bound, and [lem-kun-rgamma-unbounded-bounded] identifies this construction with the bounded derived global sections. Since $Y$ is qcqs, [lem-kun-0f0e] makes $r$ invertible for $(K,A)$. Finally $\ell$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], so no tensor boundedness theorem is needed.

For (b), again $q$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability], and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ is a torsion ring since $n1_\Lambda=0$. Thus [lem-kun-0f0g] applied to $(q,F,K)$ makes $t$ invertible without boundedness conditions. The unbounded proper base change statement [lem-kun-0f0c] applies to $(f,g,E)$ and makes $e$ invertible. The affine singleton $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring has only the ideals $(0),(1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], the finite-type scheme $Y$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], it is also quasi-separated. Since $k$ is separably closed, clause (2) of [lem-kun-0f10] gives $\kuncd(Y)<\infty$. Apply [lem-kun-0f12] on $Y$, to $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $A\in D(\Lambda)$, to conclude that $r$ is invertible. No finite Tor amplitude or boundedness is required of either object. The entire unbounded Leray comparison $\ell$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. This is the same derived composition arrow as the finite-cohomological-dimension Leray presentation in the imported statement. The stated invertibility of $n$ in $k$ is retained, although these one-proper-factor inputs do not need it.

In both cases the morphisms $s,e,t,\ell$ are isomorphisms by steps 8--11 and the symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. The symmetry squares to the identity: on bidegree $(i,j)$ the two signs multiply to $(-1)^{ij+ji}=1$, first on the tensor models and then by the descent argument of step 4. Therefore
$$s^{-1}=\sigma_{B,A}\circ r^{-1}\circ R_g(\sigma_{L_gA,K}).$$
Reverse the displayed factorization $\lambda=\ell^{-1}R_g(t)R_g(e\otimes1)s$. Its inverse is
$$\lambda^{-1}=s^{-1}R_g(e^{-1}\otimes1)R_g(t^{-1})\ell,$$
which, after substituting the preceding formula for $s^{-1}$, is exactly the stated $\theta$. Functoriality and tensor bifunctoriality take inverse pairs to inverse pairs, so cancellation gives $\theta\lambda=1$ and $\lambda\theta=1$. Step 7 identifies $\lambda$ with $\kappa_{E,K}$, proving both the required identity and the isomorphism assertion. Notice that the adjoint being compared was that of $\lambda:A\otimes B\to R_cT$, not that of $\theta\kappa:A\otimes B\to A\otimes B$.
